```{r reduction-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)
```

After finding a repeatable failure, a smaller input can make its cause
easier to understand. Removing arbitrary samples from paired data can
break the experimental design. `reduce_paired_failure()` removes genes
and whole pairs while checking that the same failure remains.

This independent recipe uses a **deliberately faulty function and synthetic
data**. It illustrates the reduction workflow, not a known bug in an
analysis package or a biological result. Install the [GitHub development
build](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel), SummarizedExperiment
and testthat before running these blocks.

## Create a paired input

There are four genes and three subjects, each measured before and after.
The integer counts make the expected result easy to inspect.

```{r paired-data}
samples <- data.frame(
  subject = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), times = 2L),
  visit = rep(c("before", "after"), each = 3L),
  row.names = paste0("sample", seq_len(6L))
)
counts <- matrix(seq_len(24L), nrow = 4L,
                 dimnames = list(paste0("gene", seq_len(4L)), rownames(samples)))
x <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = counts), colData = samples
)
dim(x)
```

## Identify the failure we want to keep

This faulty function silently discards counts of 24 or larger. On the
original data it returns 276, whereas adding all counts gives 300.

```{r faulty-operation}
count_total <- function(data) {
  counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(data, "counts")
  sum(counts[counts < 24L])
}
c(observed = count_total(x), expected = 300L)
```

The checker runs the operation on each candidate subset and returns a
stable identifier for this particular discrepancy. `NULL` means the
discrepancy is absent. An unexpected error is allowed to stop reduction;
it should not be mistaken for the failure we are trying to preserve.

```{r failure-checker}
check_total <- function(data) {
  expected <- sum(SummarizedExperiment::assay(data, "counts"))
  if (count_total(data) != expected) return("count total loses values")
  NULL
}
check_total(x)
```

## Reduce and inspect the result

Use the subject column to identify pairs and the visit column to identify
conditions. The design must be additive, with both columns as main effects.
Here it is `~ subject + visit`.

```{r reduce-input}
reduced <- biocroxytest::reduce_paired_failure(
  x, pair = "subject", condition = "visit", design = ~ subject + visit,
  check = check_total, seed = 42L
)
rbind(original = dim(x), reduced = dim(reduced$data))
reduced$failure
SummarizedExperiment::assay(reduced$data, "counts")
```

The result has one gene and four samples: two complete pairs. One pair
alone would leave no residual degrees of freedom for this design. Verify
the pair structure, the design, and the identity of the retained failure:

```{r verify-reduction}
metadata <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(reduced$data))
table(metadata$subject, metadata$visit)
model <- stats::model.matrix(~ subject + visit, metadata)
stopifnot(
  identical(dim(reduced$data), c(1L, 4L)),
  all(table(metadata$subject, metadata$visit) == 1L),
  qr(model)$rank == ncol(model), nrow(model) > ncol(model),
  identical(check_total(reduced$data), check_total(x))
)
```

## Turn the smaller input into a regression test

Keep the expected correct behavior in the test. First verify that the
faulty function fails that assertion. `expect_failure()` is used here
only to demonstrate the old defect without stopping the tutorial. The
four displayed counts, 8, 12, 20 and 24, add up to 64.

```{r demonstrate-regression}
fixture <- reduced$data
expected <- 64L
testthat::expect_identical(as.integer(SummarizedExperiment::assay(fixture)),
                           c(8L, 12L, 20L, 24L))
testthat::expect_failure(testthat::expect_identical(count_total(fixture), expected))
```

Correct the operation by summing all values. The same assertion now
passes, and the checker no longer reports the failure.

```{r correct-operation}
count_total <- function(data) sum(SummarizedExperiment::assay(data, "counts"))
testthat::expect_identical(count_total(fixture), expected)
stopifnot(is.null(check_total(fixture)))
```

For a permanent regression test, save the reviewed fixture in your test
data directory and keep the `expect_identical()` assertion with an
independently checked expected value. Include the data creation or source
and the reason this input matters. The [fixture recipe](test-fixtures.html)
shows how to identify the saved bytes.

## Boundaries of the reducer

The current reducer supports exactly two conditions and one observation
per condition in every pair. It preserves a full-rank additive design and
positive residual degrees of freedom. Put any additional scientific
constraints, such as a minimum number of subjects per group, in your checker.

Reduction is a bounded greedy search, not a guarantee of the smallest
possible input. Inspect `reduced$checks` and `reduced$budget_exhausted` if
you set `max_checks`. The checker must be repeatable; the same base R seed
is used for every attempt. Set seeds for other random-number generators
inside the checker when needed.

An HDF5-backed subset retains its backing file. Saving the subset with
`saveRDS()` alone does not make that file portable. Review and reload any
exported data, and verify the same failure before sharing it.
